questions.prompt: What is the core move of exit strategy in this chapter?
choices: Leave only when every possible value has been extracted
Leave while workable terms still exist instead of waiting for collapse
Treat any discomfort as proof that the campaign should end

explanation.gentle: The chapter defines exit strategy as timely withdrawal, not as maximum extraction or emotional quitting.
explanation.direct: Start with the timing rule: the operator leaves before the remaining options decay into worse terms.
explanation.competitive: This move is about walking through the good door before it rots.

questions.prompt: Why do precommitted exit conditions matter?
choices: Because they remove all need for later judgment
Because they protect decisions from sunk cost, pride, and identity drift
Because they guarantee teams will never argue about timing

explanation.gentle: The chapter treats stop conditions as a way to guard judgment before the campaign becomes emotionally fused with the self.
explanation.direct: Keep the purpose clear: exit triggers exist to resist later distortion, not to abolish thinking.
explanation.competitive: Write the stop line before pride starts redrawing the map.

questions.prompt: What is the main reversal attached to exit strategy?
choices: Persistence is always superior to withdrawal
Once stop conditions are written, they should never be questioned
Some apparent exit signals are false and require judgment

explanation.gentle: The chapter warns that not every painful phase is true decline.
explanation.direct: Notice the limit: a hard stretch can be temporary, so exit strategy still needs a current reading of reality.
explanation.competitive: Not every ugly mile is the end of the road.

questions.prompt: Mireya has one more quarter available, but the initiative has already hit the stop conditions. Which choice fits the chapter best?
choices: Honor the stop conditions and exit while losses are still containable
Stay automatically because more time always clarifies things
Ignore the conditions because the team feels committed

explanation.gentle: Mireya's case is about leaving before the wider system absorbs more damage.
explanation.direct: Apply the rule cleanly: once the exit case is met, one more cycle of hope is not a strategic answer by itself.
explanation.competitive: Do not buy a fourth loss to prove you cared.

questions.prompt: Stellan says the team should stop talking about how much time has already gone in. What should replace that question?
choices: Whether the team still feels emotionally attached
What one more round is likely to cost and return from here
How embarrassing it would be to end now

explanation.gentle: He is shifting the room from sunk effort to present expected value.
explanation.direct: Use the marginal test: past investment is history, while the decision depends on current cost and likely return.
explanation.competitive: Make the next mile justify itself.

questions.prompt: Cosima sees the failing product beginning to damage stronger work around it. What does the chapter suggest?
choices: That systemic spillover is a serious reason to consider exit now
That spillover does not matter if the team is determined
That she should wait until the product fails completely on its own

explanation.gentle: The chapter asks operators to protect the wider field, not just the troubled campaign.
explanation.direct: Read the containment problem accurately: once losses spread outward, the cost of staying rises sharply.
explanation.competitive: Cut the leak before it floods the ship.

questions.prompt: Bram wants to leave a difficult phase immediately, but the evidence is mixed and the pain may be temporary. Which judgment fits the chapter?
choices: Leave now because discomfort is enough
Stay forever because persistence proves character
Test whether the stop case is structural before calling retreat disciplined

explanation.gentle: This is the reversal in action. Temporary pain is not automatically a real exit trigger.
explanation.direct: Separate evidence of structural decline from the urge to escape discomfort before you call the withdrawal strategic.
explanation.competitive: Make the field prove it is dead before you bury the campaign.

questions.prompt: Ivara hears a team defend its proposal mostly by citing all the work already invested. What is the best diagnosis?
choices: The team is probably reading sunk cost as future value
The team has proved the proposal deserves more time
The team is showing the right kind of seriousness

explanation.gentle: Accumulated effort can feel persuasive even when it says little about the value of continuing.
explanation.direct: Name the distortion precisely: prior investment is being used as evidence for future return when it is only evidence of past cost.
explanation.competitive: They are letting the bill impersonate the forecast.

questions.prompt: Where is the ethical line in exit strategy?
choices: It is crossed whenever someone leaves before full collapse
It is crossed when exit language is used either to protect vanity persistence or to escape evidence-free discomfort
It is crossed only when public embarrassment is involved

explanation.gentle: The chapter resists both identity-driven staying and fear-driven leaving, asking for disciplined judgment instead.
explanation.direct: Hold both errors in view: vanity persistence and cowardly retreat are opposite corruptions of the same decision.
explanation.competitive: The moral break comes when ego or relief, not evidence, starts steering the exit.

questions.prompt: Why does the book move from exit strategy in Chapter 22 into dirtier warfare in Chapter 23?
choices: Because once you learn to exit, moral restraint is no longer needed
Because exit strategy fails whenever unconventional tactics appear
Because the book closes the conventional section with restraint before entering a section where overreach becomes easier to rationalize

explanation.gentle: The transition matters because Chapter 22 ends on disciplined restraint before the ethical temperature rises sharply.
explanation.direct: Track the structural shift: the next section rewards asymmetry and dirtier moves, so the book places exit discipline just before that pressure begins.
explanation.competitive: The last clean lesson arrives right before the book starts tempting you to get filthy.
